text:
marie: Quick signal — we've got steady memory growth on Dedicated p0 GPUs for long chat contexts (~60k tokens). Doesn't show up on hosted. :eyes:

vishal: Can you share node/kernel/build info and a small smaps/vmstat snapshot? Hosted and Dedicated configs might differ (jemalloc, THP, kernel version).

marie: Yep. Dedicated node: rtx-a2-48, kernel 5.15.0-70, jemalloc 5.2.1. Hosted instance (same model): kernel 6.1.0, jemalloc 5.3.0. Short dump below (truncated):

```
$ vmstat 1 3
procs -----------memory---------- ---swap-- -----io---- -system-- ------cpu-----
 r  b   swpd   free   buff  cache   si   so    bi    bo   in   cs us sy id wa st
 2  0  123456  204800 51200 1048576  0    0    50    10  1200  900 12 4 84 0 0
```

sasha: Can you also paste a pmap/smaps of the process when RSS climbs? Need to see anon vs file-backed growth.

marie: smaps shows rising AnonHugePages and Private_Dirty on the kv cache region. Looks like pages are being pinned rather than reclaimed. On hosted same workload shows more SwapOut/shorter KV lifespan.

jake: Interesting. Dedicated 5.15 kernel might have different THP/madvise behavior. Are we using madvise(MADV_HUGEPAGE) anywhere? Also check /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled.

marie: THP is "always" on dedicated, "madvise" on hosted. We do not explicitly madvise in runtime. That could cause fragmentation of k-v frames when pages are coalesced.

olivia: Also check network MTU for VPC — packetization affects batching and request interleaving; I've seen different KV reuse patterns when requests are bundled vs when they arrive one-by-one. Not likely the mem growth root but worth noting.

perf-bot: perf sample attached (top flame summary): high samples in "kv_cache_eviction_scan" and "page_fault_handler+0x..."; heavy spin in reclaim path.

marie: Putting repro steps here:
1) Start a dedicated p0 replica with long-context chat generator config (max_context=65536, batcher=continuous)
2) Feed ~2.5k long sessions that append tokens over time
3) Observe RSS over 6 hours, track /proc/*/smaps change every 10m

```
# simplified repro script
for i in $(seq 1 2500); do
  curl -s -X POST $DEDICATED_API -d '{"prompt":"long chat...","append":true}' &
  sleep 0.1
done
```

vishal: Good. Hypotheses: (A) THP coalescing on Dedicated turns many small kv frames into huge pages which are then harder to evict leading to Private_Dirty growth, (B) jemalloc version differences cause different fragmentation patterns and tcache behavior, (C) kernel page reclaim/backoff paths differ between 5.15 vs 6.1 causing more minor page faults and slower reclaim on Dedicated.

sasha: Another angle: batching heuristics. If Dedicated batcher groups more requests into the same worker due to throughput settings, the same KV frames stay hotter and pinned; when not reused they leak on the worker. Compare batching histograms between envs (batch sizes, idle flush thresholds).

jake: Add perf counters for LRU hits/evict scans and track "kv_slot_touch" events. If scan rate >> touch rate, eviction is scanning too aggressively or missing coalesced frames.

marie: I captured a short perf timeline and a jemalloc stats dump. Key bits: arena fragmentation rises, active vs allocated gap grows over time. jemalloc shows large counts of small extents being retained.

perf-bot: jemalloc stats summary: "narenas: 4, active: 3.8G, allocated: 4.6G, retained: 1.1G" (Dedicated) vs "active: 3.2G, allocated: 3.4G, retained: 200M" (hosted).

olivia: That retained delta is huge. Try setting MALLOC_CONF="oversize_threshold:1,dirty_decay_ms:10000,muzzy_decay_ms:10000" on dedicated and see if retained drops. Also try setting MALLOC_CONF to disable tcache per-thread to measure effect.

marie: Will try. Also going to toggle /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled -> "madvise" and retest.

vishal: For on-prem/private deployments, note GPUs often come with older kernels and different iommu/hugepage defaults. We should document recommended kernel/jemalloc combos for Dedicated vs Private so customers avoid config drift.

sasha: Agreed. Proposal: add a diagnostics probe in the runtime that reports (kernel version, /proc/sys/vm settings, THP state, jemalloc version, MALLOC_CONF, batcher params, KV cache stats) at startup and expose via metrics. That way support can correlate mem growth alerts with env config.

marie: Quick test results: setting THP->madvise on Dedicated lowered Private_Dirty accumulation by ~40% over 4h. MALLOC_CONF tweaks reduced retained pages by ~60%. Not a full fix but big improvement.

jake: Nice. Next steps: (1) bake MALLOC_CONF recommended settings into Dedicated base image, (2) add runtime probe + metric, (3) run a 24h A/B with THP toggled and jemalloc pinned to 5.3.0 on a canary pool.

marie: I'll open a PR with the probe + a runbook for ops. Also adding a perf regression test to eng-releases CI that compares eviction scan rates across kernel versions with synthetic long-context streams.

olivia: @oncall FYI — if anyone spots a dedicated node with similar RSS trend, tag this thread.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: kvcache-jemalloc-tuning -> canary-1 at 2026-03-19T22:00Z.

vishal: Thanks team. If marie posts the PR link I'll pick up the CI perf test work. :thumbsup:

marie: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/runtime/pulls/512 — includes probe + MALLOC_CONF proposal + test harness. I'll drop logs and raw perf data there.

sasha: Great, will review. One more note: for Private (on-prem) customers, include guidance to align THP and jemalloc or to pin config in their deployment manifests to avoid drift.

marie: Agreed. Closing loop after 24h canary. Thanks everyone. :)
